name: sol_basics_pu_6
description: Unprotected selfdestruct or arbitrary delegatecall in upgradeable implementation contract
question: The source file in `source` defines a proxy-upgradeable implementation contract that contains a `selfdestruct` call or a `delegatecall` to a caller-supplied or otherwise untrusted address reachable by unprivileged users, allowing the implementation to be destroyed or its storage/logic hijacked, thereby bricking or corrupting all proxies pointing to it, excluding cases where such calls are absent, are restricted solely to a trusted owner/admin via access control as an intentional documented kill-switch, or target fixed, hardcoded trusted addresses.
criteria: A public or external function calls `selfdestruct(address)` with no access-control modifier restricting the caller
A function performs `address(target).delegatecall(data)` where `target` or `data` is taken directly from function arguments without validation
An implementation contract exposes a callback or fallback that forwards arbitrary user-supplied calldata via `delegatecall` to an address read from a user-controlled mapping or storage slot
A library or logic contract meant to be used via `delegatecall` from a proxy itself contains a `selfdestruct` instruction reachable by any external caller
